Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

control verb and noun

direct, run, steer

also be in control, under control, have control of, keep under control, out of control, operate (a machine)

classical

Cic. Sen. 37: tantam domum … Appius regēbat
Liv. 35.11: impotentēs regendī equī (Lewis & Short)

regō, regere, rēxī, rēctum

verb, third conjugation · Conjugation on Wiktionary

control, guide, run

Of steering a ship or a horse, running a house, governing a people: whatever needs a hand on it to go straight.

Other words

  • moderor, moderārī, moderātus sum — control, manage, guide

    verb, first conjugation, deponent; with the accusative · also used · classical · Caes. BG 4.33.3: brevī moderārī ac flectere; Cic. Fam. 2.7.1: ut omnia gubernēs et moderēre prūdentiā tuā · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    With the dative it means “hold back” (see control, hold back).

  • gubernō, gubernāre, gubernāvī, gubernātum — steer; direct, manage

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 2.7.1: ut omnia gubernēs · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Properly the helmsman’s word (Greek κυβερνάω); figuratively of running affairs, a favourite with Cicero (Lewis & Short).

  • potestās, potestātis f. — power, control

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Phil. 6.4: ut sit in senātūs populīque Rōmānī potestāte (Lewis & Short); Traupman 150; Traupman 296 · Declension on Wiktionary

    “Under control”, “in someone’s control”: in potestāte esse, habēre.

  • effrēnātus, effrēnāta, effrēnātum — out of control, unbridled

    also used · classical · Liv. 37.41.10: velut effrēnātī passim incertō cursū ferrentur; Traupman 150; Traupman 296 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Properly of horses without a bridle; of people and passions, a favourite word of Cicero (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • quattuor rōbustōs fīliōs, quīnque fīliās, tantam domum, tantās clientēlās Appius regēbat et caecus et senex

    four strong sons, five daughters, so great a household, so many clients: Appius kept them all under control, blind and old as he wasCic. Sen. 37

  • tantum ūsū cotīdiānō et exercitātiōne efficiunt utī in dēclīvī ac praecipitī locō incitātōs equōs sustinēre et brevī moderārī ac flectere … cōnsuērint

    by daily use and practice they get so good that on a steep slope they can hold their galloping horses, and control and turn them in a momentCaes. BG 4.33.3

See also in charge, control, remote control, button, government.
